description: Typed divergent blocks propagate through required subexpressions without changing their tail types.
An unreachable tail still determines the block type and must match its expected type.
Divergence does not skip name resolution in unreachable statements.
A divergent right operand of a short-circuit operator is not required on every path.
A single divergent if branch does not make an if statement diverge.
A while body may not run, even when the body itself diverges.
Even an unreachable break with a normal operand prevents loop divergence under the syntactic rule.
A function call keeps its declared result type; divergence is determined locally in each body.
A loop body must have a unit-compatible tail even when that tail is unreachable.
